newsitem.title: CANADA: Starbucks, Vancouver union agree contract.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks, Vancouver union agree contract.

text.p: Starbucks Corp and the union representing 110 workers in Vancouver reached agreement in principle Thursday on a two-year labor contract, the first union accord at the coffee retailer's 1,100 outlets worldwide.

"The parties have reached agreement on a two-year collective agreement effective July 1. Both parties are unanimously recommending to their principals acceptance of the package," British Columbia Labor Relations Board mediator Brian Foley said.
Further details on the agreement will not be released until it is ratified, likely in the next few days, he said.

The 110 employees, represented by the Canadian Auto Workers union, work at eight coffee bars and a bakery distribution center in Vancouver. Last year they became the first locations in the Starbucks chain to be unionized.
The two sides have been negotiating for months on their first contract.
Workers at the distribution center, which has been slated for closure, went on strike in late May and this halted deliveries of baked goods to Vancouver area Starbucks stores.
The main issues in the negotiations had been wages and work flexibility. The union was demanding a starting wage of C$10 an hour compared to C$7 currently.
Foley said the collective agreement provides severance pay and retraining for workers at the distribution center.
